title: Confound Detective
summary: Classify the variables in three fictional studies as confounds, nuisance, manipulation or held constant. Then repair each design and watch the estimated effect move back towards the truth.
learningObjectives: State the two conditions a variable must meet before it can bias a comparison.
Distinguish a confound from a nuisance variable, from part of the manipulation and from a constant.
Explain why increasing sample size fixes noise and cannot fix bias.
Compare what randomisation and statistical adjustment each require in order to work.
Choose a design repair that removes a named bias rather than one that only improves precision.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native selects, checkboxes and buttons, each with an explicit label and grouped in a fieldset with a legend. The causal diagram is hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table giving every confound, its status in words - open, partly blocked with a percentage, or blocked - and the bias it is contributing; blocked nodes in the diagram carry a dashed outline and the word 'blocked' inside the node as well as a muted stroke. The two effect bars print their own name and their own number, and are distinguished by a stripe pattern as well as by fill. The study card and, once the repair bench opens, the estimate are pinned to the top of the stage so both stay visible while the controls below are worked through. Every repair announces a full sentence including the new estimate through the polite live region. Reduced motion is honoured for the bar transitions, forced-colours rules are provided for every diagram and bar class, focus moves to the detective heading when it unlocks, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Confounds, nuisance variables and design repair: why more data cannot fix bias
simulationNotes: Three invented studies - a revision app, a hospital ward audit and a typeface experiment - covering between-groups confounding, confounding by indication in observational data, and order and material confounds in a within-participants design. Each study has a true effect known only to the tool plus a fixed bias per confound; the estimate is the true effect plus the sum of the unblocked biases. A repair removes a stated fraction of a named confound's bias, and fractions from several repairs combine multiplicatively rather than adding. Precision is tracked separately as a multiplier on interval width, so noise and bias move independently on screen. One repair in every study blocks nothing and only improves precision. The bias figures are invented to make the argument legible and are not estimates of confounding in any real study; real confounds interact and sometimes cancel, and keeping them additive here is a deliberate simplification. No real module, ward, trial, patient or dataset is described.
